
5s-Block Quadruple-Zeta Basis Set Archive
=========================================


Date: 22 Jun 2006


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, in preparation. Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF orbital coefficients, given with
respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for the basis
sets described in the above articles. The SCF exponent sets reported include the
functions for the 5p and the valence correlating d functions. The d sets were
reoptimized after replacement of the outermost two SCF d functions with the three
valence correlating d functions, which were held fixed.  In all the following
descriptions, this is the set referred to as the SCF exponent set.

The contractions are taken from SCF calculations on a weighted average of the
5s^n and 5p^n configurations, with a weight ratio of 4:1.

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of 5s5p correlating functions.

4. Exponents of 4s4p correlating functions.

5. Exponents of 3d correlating functions.

6. Exponents of 4s4p polarizing functions


Basis set construction.
----------------------

For the s elements, the outer core (n-1)s and (n-1)p must be included in the
valence.  For Sr, the valence np is considered an occupied orbital and is
correlated; hence there are extra correlating functions for Sr.

Several different types of basis sets may be constructed by adding primitive 
functions to the SCF set. These basis sets are described below.

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 

1. Valence and outer core. To the SCF occupied set, add the following:
   1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 8th s primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 8th p primitives from the SCF set
   4s4p correlating 3d2f1g set (includes 1st-3rd d primitives from the SCF set)
   5s5p correlating set (2d1f for Rb, 2d1f1g for Sr)

   (HF + 6s6p5d3f1g/2g valence/outer core)


2. Core 3d correlation. To basis set 1, add the following:
   10th, 11th, and 12th s primitives from the SCF set
   9th, 10th, and 11th p primitives from the SCF set
   4th, 6th, and 7th d primitives from the SCF set
   3d correlating 3f2g1h set

   (HF + 6s6p5d3f1g/2g valence/outer core + 3s3p3d3f2g1h core)


3. Outer core (4s4p) polarization. To any of the above basis sets, add the 
   s, p, f, and g polarizing functions.





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================           




** Rb **
